chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to travel during the month of Ramadan and leaves his home after morning prayer. He said: If he is in his home at morning, fasting for that day becomes obligatory upon him, unless he departs after a late morning (delaying departure).

key_terms.دَلْجَةً: A late morning period (after Fajr but before noon)
key_terms.يُصْبِحُ: He becomes morning / morning prayer time

ai.seo_question: Does a person who intends to travel in Ramadan need to fast if they leave home after Fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific condition for breaking the fast while traveling: the traveler must not have been in their home city at the time of Fajr prayer with the intention of staying. The key criterion is whether they depart before or after the time of 'Ida' al-Dalaj (late morning), which determines if they are considered a resident for that day or a traveler eligible for the concession. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the time of departure as the decisive factor for applying the rules of travel (Safar) to fasting.
